examples.claim: NVIDIA install needs Linux and Python 3.11–3.14; `vllm serve` serves at http://localhost:8000 by default
examples.source: Quickstart: 'OS: Linux Python: 3.11 -- 3.14'; 'By default, it starts the server at http://localhost:8000'; parsed default port 8000.

examples.claim: LLaMA-13B KV cache takes up to 1.7GB for a single sequence
examples.source: Blog: 'Large: Takes up to 1.7GB for a single sequence in LLaMA-13B.'

examples.claim: Up to 24x over HF; one output 14–24x HF and 2.2–2.5x TGI; three outputs 8.5–15x HF and 3.3–3.5x TGI; LLaMA-7B on A10G and LLaMA-13B on A100 40GB, ShareGPT lengths
examples.source: Blog performance section, verbatim ranges and settings.

examples.claim: LMSYS moved Chatbot Arena/Vicuna to FastChat-vLLM (April–May 2023), cut GPUs by 50%, 30K requests/day average and 60K peak
examples.source: Blog: 'Since mid-April ... FastChat-vLLM integration'; 'between April to May'; 'cut the number of GPUs ... by 50%. vLLM has been handling an average of 30K requests daily and a peak of 60K'.

examples.claim: Blockwise attention: A_ij = exp(q_i^T K_j/√d) / Σ_t exp(q_i^T K_t 1/√d), o_i = Σ_j V_j A_ij^T over ⌈i/B⌉ blocks
examples.source: Paper §4.1 Eq. (4), same symbols and bounds.

examples.claim: In the paper's example a block holds 4 tokens and the prompt is 7 tokens
examples.source: Paper §4.3 / Fig. 6 ('block size of 4', 7-token prompt 'Four score and seven years ago our').

examples.claim: Parallel sampling: both samples map logical 0, 1 to physical 7, 1 with refcount 2; A1's write allocates block 3 and copies, refcount drops to 1, A2 writes in place
examples.source: Paper §4.4 parallel sampling walk-through, same block numbers.

examples.claim: Beam k=4: each candidate has 4 full logical blocks; all share block 0; candidate 3 diverges at the second block; 0–2 share three blocks and diverge at the fourth
examples.source: Paper §4.4: 'each candidate sequence has used 4 full logical blocks. All beam candidates share the first block 0 ... Candidate 3 digresses from others from the second block. Candidates 0-2 share the first 3 blocks and diverge at the fourth block.'

examples.claim: Sharing cuts parallel-sampling/beam memory by up to 55%, and the 3-parallel-completion HF/TGI benchmark numbers are exactly this case
examples.source: 55% is verbatim; the blog links it to 'up to 2.2x improvement in throughput', not to the 8.5–15x / 3.3–3.5x system comparison.

examples.claim: Swapping: after preempting, vLLM accepts no new requests until preempted sequences finish; CPU swap space bounded by GPU KV memory; recomputation rebuilds all positions in one prompt iteration
examples.source: Paper §4.5: 'vLLM stops accepting new requests until all preempted sequences are completed'; 'the swap space on the CPU RAM is bounded by the GPU memory allocated for the KV cache'; 'their KV cache at all positions can be generated in one prompt phase iteration'.

examples.claim: --gpu-memory-utilization is a per-instance 0–1 fraction; two instances on one GPU use 0.5 each; unset -> 1.0 with extensible KV cache, else 0.92
examples.source: Engine args: 'This is a per-instance limit ...'; 'If unspecified, 1.0 with the extensible KV cache (sized from measured memory) and 0.92 otherwise'.

examples.claim: CPU tuning: --max-num-batched-tokens affects first-token, --max-num-seqs output-token performance; defaults 4096/2048 × world_size and 256/128 × world_size (offline/online)
examples.source: CPU page performance tuning, verbatim defaults.

examples.claim: Decimal suffixes allow fractions (25.6k = 25,600), binary suffixes integers only (32K = 32,768); five suffix arguments listed
examples.source: CLI page: 'Decimal suffixes (k, m, g, t) also accept floating point: 25.6k = 25,600. Binary suffixes (K, M, G, T) require integers: 32K = 32,768. Supported arguments include: --max-model-len, --max-num-batched-tokens, --max-num-scheduled-tokens, --kv-cache-memory-bytes, --safetensors-prefetch-block-size'.

examples.claim: When the preemption counter keeps rising, lower --max-num-seqs, enlarge KV capacity or add instances via HPA
examples.source: runpod: 'reduce --max-model-len, raise --gpu-memory-utilization, or add capacity'; --max-num-seqs is the writer's.

examples.claim: A rising preemption counter signals a batch cap that is high relative to KV cache capacity
examples.source: Not stated in any source; a cause the writer adds.

off_sample_findings.claim: A 'third-party post introducing V1' reports hash-based prefix caching with LRU in V0 and V1 and <1% throughput loss at 0% hit rate
off_sample_findings.source: The source is the official vLLM blog 'vLLM V1: A Major Upgrade to vLLM's Core Architecture' (2025-01-27, vLLM team): 'vLLM V1, like V0, uses hash-based prefix caching and LRU-based cache eviction ... less than 1% decrease in throughput even when the cache hit rate is 0%'. Numbers right, attribution wrong.

off_sample_findings.claim: Against current serving engines, take the paper's 2–4x as the realistic starting point
off_sample_findings.source: Paper: 2–4x vs FasterTransformer and Orca (2022-2023 systems). No source compares vLLM with current engines; this is the writer's extrapolation presented as guidance.

off_sample_findings.claim: The 60–80% waste comes exactly from this kind of reservation
off_sample_findings.source: Blog: 'waste 60% – 80% of memory due to fragmentation and over-reservation'; paper adds external fragmentation and missed sharing. The sentence narrows the cause to reservation.

off_sample_findings.claim: nm-vllm 0.5.0 docs say the KV cache block count is affected by --gpu-memory-utilization
off_sample_findings.source: nm-vllm 0.5.0 engine_args: only 'The fraction of GPU memory to be used for the model executor ... Default: 0.9' and '--num-gpu-blocks-override: If specified, ignore GPU profiling result'; no statement about block count.

off_sample_findings.claim: Swapping back can take hundreds of ms
off_sample_findings.source: runpod: 'On a PCIe 4.0 x16 link (~32 GB/s), restoring a long-context sequence on Llama-3-70B can take hundreds of milliseconds'; the post drops model, link and context scope (L225, L229).
Docker docs: 'You can either use the ipc=host flag or --shm-size flag'; the post's next sentence says the same, so the first sentence overstates.
